column2:
shlōnik?
EN: how are you?
Her word, lit. "what's your colour"; older Riyadh: وش لونك

ēh
EN: yes
Careful: in Egyptian إيه means "what"
⚠ check with tutor

abshir / abshiri
EN: consider it done (to him / to her)
Very Saudi

tara
EN: you know, look…
Softener at the start of a sentence

kēfik?
EN: how are you?
To her; to him kēfak

shakhbārik?
EN: what's new? how are you?
Her word

tislam
EN: thanks
To him — what she'll say to you

allah yiʿṭīk al-ʿāfya
EN: "God give you strength"
When she's worked or done something

w inti min ahlah
EN: reply to good night
To her; she says وانت to you

mā shāʾ allah
EN: wow, great
Praise that also wards off the evil eye

ḥēl
EN: very
Older Najdi — young people say مرة

marra
EN: very / once
The everyday Saudi "very": حلو مرة — really nice
